original_question: Let (Omega, mu) be a sigma-finite measure space, let V be a dense subspace of L2(Omega), let a: V x V -> C be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form, let -A generate the associated bounded analytic semigroup (T(t)) on L2(Omega), and assume that (T(t)) is L-infinity-bounded. Characterize exactly when there exists a function g in L-infinity(Omega) with g > 0 mu-almost everywhere and 1/g in L-infinity(Omega) such that ||g T(t)f||_infinity <= ||g f||_infinity for all f in L2(Omega) intersect L-infinity(Omega) and all t >= 0.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 23 (Characterization of L∞-contraction for a weight), with the setup and notation inherited from Problem 21.
correct_elements: The draft already identifies the correct part of the paper: the Section 6 form-method setting on a σ-finite measure space, with V dense in L2(Ω), a closed sectorial complex sesquilinear form a, the associated bounded analytic semigroup (T(t)) on L2(Ω), the extra assumption of L∞-boundedness, and the search for a weight g in L∞(Ω) with g>0 μ-a.e. and 1/g in L∞(Ω) such that the weighted sup norm is contractive. That is the content of Problem 23 rather than the unconditional existence question of Problem 22.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the question should explicitly define L∞-boundedness as: there exists M≥1 such that ||T(t)f||∞ ≤ M||f||∞ for every t≥0 and every f in L2(Ω)∩L∞(Ω).
It should explicitly say that A is the operator associated with the form a in the sense of Problem 21, rather than only referring informally to the 'associated semigroup'.

It should make clear that the task is to characterize those L∞-bounded semigroups in this form-theoretic setting for which such a weight exists; otherwise the draft can be misread as Problem 22, which asks whether every L∞-bounded semigroup has such a weight.

If one wants the paper's own sharp reformulation, one should mention the equivalent norm viewpoint from the comments to Problem 23: contractivity on the ||·||∞-closure of L2(Ω)∩L∞(Ω) in L∞(Ω) for an equivalent norm specifically of the form f ↦ ||gf||∞.
refined_question: Let (Ω,μ) be a σ-finite measure space, let V be a dense subspace of L2(Ω) of complex-valued functions, and let a:V×V→ℂ be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form, linear in the first argument and antilinear in the second. Let A be the operator on L2(Ω) associated with a, so that -A generates the bounded analytic semigroup (T(t))t≥0 on L2(Ω). Assume that (T(t))t≥0 is L∞-bounded, i.e. there exists M≥1 such that ||T(t)f||∞ ≤ M||f||∞ for all t≥0 and all f∈L2(Ω)∩L∞(Ω). Characterize precisely those such L∞-bounded semigroups for which there exists a function g∈L∞(Ω) with g>0 μ-almost everywhere and 1/g∈L∞(Ω) such that ||gT(t)f||∞ ≤ ||gf||∞ for all t≥0 and all f∈L2(Ω)∩L∞(Ω).
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, characterize precisely when (T(t))t≥0 can be made into a contractive semigroup on the ||·||∞-closure of L2(Ω)∩L∞(Ω) in L∞(Ω) by an equivalent norm of the special form f ↦ ||gf||∞, where g∈L∞(Ω), g>0 μ-a.e., and 1/g∈L∞(Ω).
justification: The draft is not aiming at the paper's opening generation problems or any Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3-type material; it clearly matches Section 6 on L∞-bounds. Problem 21 supplies the exact ambient hypotheses, the definition of L∞-boundedness in equation (1), and the weighted contractivity condition (3) on page 15. Problem 22 on page 16 asks the stronger blanket existence question for every L∞-bounded semigroup. Your draft instead asks for an exact characterization of when such a weight exists under the Problem 21 assumptions, which is exactly the wording and intent of Problem 23 on page 16. The comments to Problem 23 provide the paper's only explicit equivalent reformulation, namely the renorming statement with a norm of the special form f↦||gf||∞. Problem 24 and its comments on page 17 are downstream questions about constructing such a weight and about positivity-based heuristics, so they should not replace Problem 23 as the main target.
